narrative.overview:
Every AI draft is a proof lying on an editor's desk. The interface is cool newsprint (#F0F0EB) with whiter proof slips on it, ink-black type, and a single blue editing pencil for actions and focus. Structure comes from hairline rules and tonal steps between paper and slip, not from boxes and shadows. It is a working tool for long sessions, in daylight: dense, quiet, legible.

The build is light only, by decision: the scene is a daylight office, so color-scheme: light is set and no dark theme exists. The serif face appears only where words are being edited or read as copy; everything else is the grotesk. Icons are authored SVG that borrow proofreader's marks.
keyCharacteristics: Newsprint ground, proof-slip surfaces, hairline dividers.
One accent (pencil blue) for every action and focus ring; red is reserved for urgency, rejection, errors.
Two faces with a strict job split: grotesk for interface, serif for edited words.
Flat at rest; one soft slip shadow on the draft and the home specimen only.
Priority and status always carry a word, never color alone.

rules.name: The One Pencil Rule
rules.body: Blue means "you can act here" or "you are here". It is the only chromatic accent for interaction.

rules.name: The Red Is a Verdict Rule
rules.body: Proof red appears only for urgent, reject and errors. Never for decoration or a second brand color.

rules.name: The Wash Pairing Rule
rules.body: Every semantic ink pairs with its own wash for backgrounds; do not put a semantic ink on paper-colored chips outside this pairing.

rules.name: The Serif Is for Edited Words Rule
rules.body: Source Serif 4 is used only for message bodies, drafts and the textareas where copy is written. Never for headings, labels or buttons.

rules.name: The Tight Headings Rule
rules.body: Headings are bold with negative tracking and text-balance; body copy stays untracked. Prose measure is capped (46-60ch) where it runs long.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Panels, rows and inputs carry a hairline, not a shadow. The slip shadow is reserved for the single proof under review on a screen.

dos: Do use pencil (#2742D1) for every primary action, focus ring and selection, and nothing else.
Do separate content with 1px hairlines (rule) and the paper/slip tonal step before reaching for a shadow.
Do set customer messages, AI drafts and copy textareas in Source Serif 4 at 17px with relaxed leading.
Do pair color with a word or mark (priority ticks plus label, status chip text).
Do keep controls at 36px on desktop and 44px on phones, with 16px field text on phones.
Do wrap entrance motion in motion-safe: and keep to the single 300ms land.
donts: Don't use proof red for anything but urgent, reject and errors.
Don't use the serif for headings, buttons, labels or navigation.
Don't add dark mode or dark surfaces; the system is light by decision.
Don't add rounded-pill chips, soft stacked cards, gradient fills, or a sparkle/AI-glow treatment for AI features.
Don't use stock icon sets; extend Icons.tsx in the same 1.7 stroke, 24px grid.
Don't put the slip shadow on ordinary panels or rows.
